eyebrow: Discount every future cash flow back to today
code:
Price = Sum[ Coupon_t / (1+y)^t ] + FaceValue / (1+y)^T

Example: $1,000 face, 6% annual coupon, 3yr, 8% YTM
Year 1:  $60   / 1.08^1 = $55.56
Year 2:  $60   / 1.08^2 = $51.44
Year 3:  $1,060/ 1.08^3 = $841.00
                  Price = $948.00
caption: The bond prices below par because its 6% coupon is below the 8% market yield.

code:
Macaulay Duration = Sum[ t x PV(CF_t) ] / Price
  = (1x55.56 + 2x51.44 + 3x841.00) / 948.00
  = 2,681.44 / 948.00 = 2.83 years

Modified Duration = Macaulay Duration / (1+y)
  = 2.83 / 1.08 = 2.62
caption: Modified duration of 2.62 means roughly a 2.62% price drop for every 1-point rise in yield.

eyebrow: The curve duration alone can't capture
code:
Delta-P / P  ~=  -D x Delta-y  +  (1/2) x C x (Delta-y)^2

  -D x Delta-y        : linear, first-order estimate
  (1/2) x C x (Delta-y)^2  : convexity correction, always >= 0
caption: Convexity cushions losses when yields rise and boosts gains when yields fall — it works in the bondholder's favor both ways.
